_: Fri 16 Oct 2026 · home slot, sober register, no joke. Sources READ 9 Oct 2026: FEMA 'Tips for returning home safely after a disaster' (fema.gov) and Ready.gov recovering-from-disaster guidance. Used: walk around the outside before going in and check for loose power lines, gas leaks and structural damage; treat downed lines as live and report them to the power company; do not walk, drive or wade through standing water because lines can electrically charge it; if you smell gas or hear hissing leave and call the fire department, use a flashlight not a match; if in doubt have the home looked at by a qualified building inspector or structural engineer. Written after the 10-11 Oct storm so it reads as a general check, not a live alert.
headline:
Walk The Outside First
Before You Go Back In
titan_line: Echo, after a big storm FEMA says to walk around the outside first and check for loose power lines, gas leaks and structural damage.
rows: Treat any downed line as live and stay away. Report it to the power company. A licensed electrician checks the rest.
Do not wade through standing water; lines can charge it. A licensed contractor handles cleanup.
If you smell gas or hear hissing, leave and call the fire department. Use a flashlight, not a match.
If the building looks unstable, a qualified inspector or engineer should look before anyone goes in.
echo_line: Outside first, then inside. I never thought to check the lines before the door.
source: FEMA and Ready.gov, returning home after a disaster · retrieved Oct 9, 2026
disclaimer: General safety information, not an inspection or advice about any home. Follow local officials and ask a licensed professional about yours.
